stages.name: Why some firms stay small
stages.title: Why some firms stay small
stages.sub: Explain the different reasons a firm might choose, or be forced, to remain small.

steps.q: A tailor makes hand-stitched wedding suits for a small, wealthy group of customers in one city. If she tried to sell mass-market suits nationwide, would her small, specialist customer base still want her products?
steps.right: No, that group is too small and specific to support mass sales
steps.wrong: Yes, everyone needs suits so she could sell nationwide
steps.hint: Think about how many people actually want hand-stitched, expensive suits.
steps.pre: A small, specialist segment of the market like this is called a

steps.q: A baker loves running her one shop herself, knowing every customer by name and setting her own hours. If she opened ten branches, could she still personally run each one and keep her lifestyle?
steps.right: No, she would have to hand over control to managers
steps.wrong: Yes, she could still run every branch herself
steps.hint: Think about what she would have to give up to expand.
steps.pre: Choosing to stay small to keep this control is an

steps.q: A small firm wants to expand output, but as it grows its average costs start rising rather than falling, and banks are also unwilling to lend it more money to invest. Can it easily keep growing?
steps.right: No, these problems make growing harder
steps.wrong: Yes, it can grow just as easily as before
steps.hint: Think about obstacles that stop a firm getting bigger, not just choices it makes.

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 3 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: One firm serves only a tiny specialist market, another firm's owner deliberately avoids expanding, and a third firm faces rising costs and difficulty borrowing. Do all three end up staying small for the same single reason?
steps.right: No, there are several different reasons firms can stay small
steps.wrong: Yes, they are all really the same reason
steps.hint: Compare a deliberate choice, a market limitation, and an obstacle to growth.
